subject: Renewal: Add reserved capacity and shift GPU class — performance-per-dollar analysis
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@cloudnova.ai>
Cc: Miguel Santos <m.santos@cloudnova.ai>
Date: 2027-01-10T08:15:00Z
Subject: Renewal planning — capacity add + hardware class question

Hi Emma / Miguel,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Per our conversation I pulled together a concise plan for CloudNova's renewal window (Mar 1, 2027 effective date) and a couple of options for hardware-class changes to improve perf/$ for your high-throughput inference workloads. High level: you currently run a Reserved Pool of 80 A100s. Based on your Q4 utilization and the 12‑month forecast you shared, our recommended paths are:

1) Preferred (throughput-focused): Convert 80 A100 -> 120 H100 reserved equivalents (same slot commitment, higher perf) + add a 40‑card H100 burst pool for steady peak headroom.
2) Cost-balanced (mixed strategy): Keep 80 A100 baseline, add 40 L40S for lower-cost batch/embedding jobs, and convert 40 of the busiest A100s to H100.

Attached: CloudNova_Q4_perf_vs_cost.xlsx — I included model-level perf estimates (tokens/sec), p50/p95 latency projections, and a simple perf-per-dollar row to show when H100 wins vs L40S by workload pattern. Also attached a proposed_reserved_schedule_2027-2028.pdf with suggested commit tiers and a draft MAP_v3_for_signature.docx.

Questions for you to unblock next steps:
- Do you have a hard mandate to reduce committed spend, or is the priority to hit a throughput target (e.g., 3M tokens/sec steady across the fleet)?
- Any procurement timing constraints we should model (PO lead time, quarter-end signoff)?

If helpful I can loop in Product/Runtime (brief technical note attached from Jonas) to walk through perf tradeoffs for long-sequence vs short-seq models.

Best,
Dylan

--
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0192

From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@cloudnova.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <m.santos@cloudnova.ai>
Date: 2027-01-12T13:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity add + hardware class question

Thanks Dylan — this is helpful. A few clarifying items from our side:

- Our SRE/infra team will prioritize steady throughput (3M tokens/sec) and predictable p95 latency under peak. Cost is important but secondary to reliability.
- Procurement timeline: we need signed terms by Feb 10 to hit April invoicing cycles.
- Can you confirm: the "120 H100 equivalent" number assumes same VM count or same effective throughput? Miguel is concerned about slot equivalency when we switch.

Also — curious about the mixed strategy. What percent of our batch embedding traffic should be routed to L40S to keep quality identical?

Emma
Principal ML Engineer, CloudNova

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@cloudnova.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <m.santos@cloudnova.ai>
Date: 2027-01-13T09:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — capacity add + hardware class question

Emma — quick technical note (attaching the short sheet into Dylan's workbook as a second tab). TL;DR: H100 delivers ~1.6–2.2x tokens/sec vs A100 on smaller seq lengths (<= 1024) depending on kernel mix and whether you use FP16 vs FP8 quantized runs. For long sequences (>= 4096) the delta narrows because memory bandwidth and KV cache behavior dominate. L40S is competitive on throughput-per-dollar for batch/embedding where you can run larger batches and can accept slightly higher p95.

Routing guidance: for mixed pools we recommend initially routing 60–70% of batch/embedding jobs to L40S (same model checkpoints) while keeping latency-sensitive short-seq chat/responses on H100. We'll set up canary traffic and quality checks (exact-match and top-k BLEU/Rouge-style metrics) for 2 weeks after cutover.

Attachment referenced: perf_microbenchmarks_jonas_tab (included inside CloudNova_Q4_perf_vs_cost.xlsx).

- Memory/kv notes: if you use very large context windows (> 8k), keep those sessions on H100 or A100 where you need bigger NVLink-attached memory; L40S has lower host-memory ceiling in our configs.

-Jonas
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@cloudnova.ai>, Miguel Santos <m.santos@cloudnova.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-15T11:04:00Z
Subject: Pricing + SLA proposal (first draft)

Emma/Miguel — looping Grace on pricing and SLA. Grace — based on the mix above, our proposal to CloudNova is:

Option A (throughput-first):
- Term: 12 months (Mar 1, 2027 – Feb 28, 2028)
- Commit: 120 H100 reserved-equivalents (preserve existing slot math, see workbook)
- Burst: additional 40 H100 burst credits available per month
- Unit price: $X per H100-month (listed in attached PDF)
- Throughput guarantee: 95% availability of committed baseline at >= 3.0M tokens/sec measured weekly; fallbacks defined to mixed pool with credits.

Option B (cost-balanced):
- Term: 12 months
- Commit: 80 A100 baseline + 40 L40S reserved for batch; convert 40 A100 slots to H100 equivalent (net H100 count ~40)
- Unit price mix shown in proposed_reserved_schedule_2027-2028.pdf
- SLA: 95% of baseline throughput at >= 2.7M tokens/sec, with pre-defined escalation and priority scheduling windows.

We can provide a 3% introductory discount on committed spend if CloudNova signs by Feb 10 and accepts our standard MAP_v3 terms (attached). Also included in the PDF: lead times (8–10 business days for dedicated pool changes), rollback plan and a two-week canary policy with automatic fallback.

Grace — any comments on the SLA wording and escalation windows?

Thanks,
Dylan

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Emma Liu <emma.liu@cloudnova.ai>
Cc: Miguel Santos <m.santos@cloudnova.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-18T15:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Pricing + SLA proposal (first draft)

Thanks Dylan. A few clarifications and tightened language for the proposal:

- SLA measurement: we'll use per-token throughput sampled in 5‑minute windows, aggregated daily; we report weekly. A breach is defined as two consecutive weekly reports below committed throughput after applying normal maintenance windows.
- Credits: for breaches we offer proportional service credits applied to the next invoice (not exceeding 20% of monthly commit value).
- Canary & rollback: 14-day canary with metrics thresholds: quality delta <= 0.5% top-1 difference on production prompts; p95 latency change <= 20%. Failure to meet canary rules triggers automatic rolling rollback to baseline assets within 24 hours.

I've added the refined SLA text into the attached proposed_reserved_schedule_2027-2028.pdf (page 4). I'm fine with the 3% early-sign discount and the Feb 10 deadline — I'll authorize that in the quote.

Grace
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

1) Emma to confirm preferred option (A or B) by Jan 26 so we can lock hardware order windows.
2) Procurement: I'll send a finalized quote and DocuSign (link below) with the 3% early-sign discount applied; target sign by Feb 10.

Thanks — excited to get this locked.

Best,
Dylan
